title: Tanker transits through Hormuz fall 18% in a week
body:
Tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz fell 18 percent in the week to 15 October compared with the previous week, according to vessel-tracking data compiled by Gulf Wire Service.

A total of 212 tankers crossed the strait during the week, down from 259 a week earlier. Shipping agents in Fujairah said several owners had delayed sailings while they reviewed security arrangements.

Container traffic was less affected, with transits down 4 percent over the same period.

title: تراجع عبور الناقلات في مضيق هرمز 18 بالمئة خلال أسبوع
body:
تراجع عدد ناقلات النفط التي عبرت مضيق هرمز بنسبة 18 بالمئة في الأسبوع المنتهي في 15 أكتوبر مقارنة بالأسبوع السابق، وفقا لبيانات تتبع السفن التي جمعتها وكالة أنباء الخليج.

وعبرت 212 ناقلة المضيق خلال الأسبوع مقابل 259 في الأسبوع الذي سبقه.

title: انخفاض حركة الناقلات عبر هرمز
body:
نقلت وكالة أنباء الخليج أن عبور الناقلات في مضيق هرمز انخفض 18 بالمئة خلال أسبوع، إذ عبرت 212 ناقلة فقط.

وقال وكلاء شحن إن بعض الملاك أجلوا رحلاتهم لمراجعة الترتيبات الأمنية.

title: Our data: Hormuz tanker crossings drop sharply
body:
Maritime Insight's own analysis of satellite position reports shows tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz fell 18 percent in the week to 15 October.

Very large crude carriers accounted for most of the decline, our analysts found, while LPG carriers kept sailing at close to normal rates.

Owners we spoke to cited higher insurance costs and longer security briefings before departure.

title: Statement on port operations and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
body:
The Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology confirms that the ports of Sohar and Duqm are operating normally and are ready to receive diverted vessels.

Vessel traffic data reviewed by the ministry show that tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz fell 18 percent over the past week.

The ministry has added 6 pilot crews at Sohar to shorten waiting times. "Omani ports remain open, safe and fully operational for all commercial shipping lines," the ministry said.

title: Oman says Sohar and Duqm ports operating normally
body:
Oman's Ministry of Transport said in a statement that the ports of Sohar and Duqm are operating normally and are ready to receive diverted vessels.

"Omani ports remain open, safe and fully operational for all commercial shipping lines," the ministry said, adding that it had added 6 pilot crews at Sohar.

title: عُمان: موانئ صحار والدقم تعمل بشكل طبيعي
body: أفادت وزارة النقل والاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات العمانية بأن ميناءي صحار والدقم يعملان بشكل طبيعي، وأنها أضافت 6 طواقم إرشاد في صحار لتقليص أوقات الانتظار.

title: Advisory for Indian-flagged vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz
body:
The Directorate General of Shipping advises all Indian-flagged vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to report their position to the Information Fusion Centre every 6 hours.

Masters should keep the Automatic Identification System switched on at all times and maintain a continuous watch on VHF channel 16.

title: Revised advisory: position reporting in the Strait of Hormuz
body:
Revising its advisory of 14 October, the Directorate General of Shipping now advises all Indian-flagged vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to report their position to the Information Fusion Centre every 4 hours.

All other instructions in the earlier advisory remain in force.

title: India tightens reporting rule for ships in Hormuz
body:
India's Directorate General of Shipping said Indian-flagged vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz must now report their position every 4 hours, tightening an advisory issued three days earlier.

Shipping lines said the change would add some work for crews but was manageable.

title: War-risk premiums climb for Gulf voyages
body:
Brokers said war-risk insurance premiums for voyages through the Strait of Hormuz rose to 0.5 percent of hull value this week.

A year ago the same cover cost about 0.05 percent, brokers in London said.

title: Insurers raise war-risk rates for Hormuz transits
body:
Underwriters said war-risk insurance premiums for voyages through the Strait of Hormuz rose to 0.7 percent of hull value this week.

Several underwriters have also shortened the period for which quotes remain valid.

title: Container line to reroute two Gulf services
body:
A major container line said it would reroute two of its Asia-Gulf services through Salalah from next week.

The company said cargo for ports inside the Gulf would be moved on by feeder vessels.

title: Navy convoy for tankers?
body:
Twelve navy ships began escorting commercial tankers through the strait on 17 October.

The report could not be confirmed with any navy.

title: Gulf shipping association urges calm
body:
The Gulf Shipping Association issued a statement on Saturday. "Members are maintaining their published schedules while monitoring the situation closely around the clock," it said.

"We urge customers to book early and to keep in close contact with their agents," the association added.

title: Association: schedules maintained
body:
In a note to customers, the regional association of shipping companies struck a calm tone. "Members are maintaining their published schedules while monitoring the situation closely around the clock," the note read.

It went on: "We urge customers to book early and to keep in close contact with their agents."

title: Support for Indian-flagged merchant vessels
body:
The Indian Navy has deployed 2 ships to the Gulf of Oman to assist Indian-flagged merchant vessels, the Directorate General of Shipping said in a press note.

Vessels needing help should contact the Information Fusion Centre.

title: India sends warships to help merchant ships
body:
The Indian Navy has deployed 2 ships to the Gulf of Oman to assist Indian-flagged merchant vessels, Indian officials told Khaleej Daily.

The officials said the deployment was precautionary.

title: Freight rates set to climb
body:
Analysts expect freight rates on Gulf routes will rise further next week as insurers reprice cover.

Spot rates for a Gulf to Asia voyage already rose by a quarter this month, analysts said.

title: Jebel Ali reports normal operations
body:
Jebel Ali port reported normal operations this week, with container volumes steady at about 290,000 TEU.

The port operator said vessel waiting times were unchanged.

title: Qatar LNG loadings continue
body:
Qatar loaded 14 LNG cargoes at Ras Laffan in the week to 14 October, in line with its normal schedule, according to shipping data compiled by Gulf Wire Service.

Buyers in Asia said deliveries were arriving on time.

title: LNG shipments from Qatar on schedule
body:
Qatar loaded 14 LNG cargoes at Ras Laffan in the week to 14 October, in line with its normal schedule, Gulf Wire Service reported, citing shipping data.

Buyers in Asia said deliveries were arriving on time.

title: India-UAE trade rises in first half
body:
Trade between India and the UAE rose 9 percent in the first half of 2026 to 46 billion dollars, officials said at a business forum in Dubai.

Officials said the comprehensive economic partnership agreement had lowered tariffs on most goods.

title: UAE, India eye more trade after strong half
body:
Trade between India and the UAE rose 9 percent in the first half of 2026, Khaleej Daily was told by officials at the Dubai forum.

Business leaders said they expected further growth in food and jewellery trade.

title: Late goal settles derby
body:
A late goal settled the derby on Monday night as the home side won 2-1 in front of 30,000 fans.

The coach praised his players for their patience.

title: City marathon draws record field
body:
A record 18,000 runners took part in the city marathon on Friday.

Organisers said the cooler weather helped.

title: Cricket: hosts win by six wickets
body:
The hosts won by six wickets with 12 balls to spare.

The opener scored an unbeaten 88.

title: New data centre opens in Abu Dhabi
body:
A new 40-megawatt data centre opened in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday.

The operator said it would serve cloud customers across the region.

title: Star spotted at film premiere
body:
A film star was spotted at a premiere in Dubai on Wednesday.

Fans gathered outside the cinema.

title: Hormuz traffic edges up
body:
Tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz rose 3 percent in the week to 1 October.

Traders said demand was steady.

body: Tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz rose 11 percent in the week to 24 October, according to vessel-tracking data compiled by Gulf Wire Service.
